title: Summer Lemonade Cupcakes
shortDescription: Bright lemon cupcakes with a fresh lemon frosting swirl, ready in 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These cupcakes taste like a cold glass of lemonade on a hot day. I tested this batch three times in my own kitchen to get the lemon flavor strong without turning the crumb bitter. Fresh lemon juice and zest go into both the cake and the frosting, so every bite has real citrus flavor. The crumb stays soft and moist thanks to buttermilk and a touch of oil. The frosting swirl uses fresh lemon juice, not just extract, for a true tart and sweet balance. A pinch of extra zest on top makes them look sunny and fresh. This is a simple recipe for backyard parties, picnics, or any warm afternoon when you want something light and citrusy.
ingredients: 2 tbsp lemon zest, plus extra for garnish
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F and line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt together in a bowl. Set aside.
Beat butter and sugar together for 2 minutes until light and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Mix in lemon juice, lemon zest, and vanilla extract until combined.
Add the flour mixture in two batches, alternating with buttermilk. Mix just until smooth.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
For frosting, beat butter until smooth, then add powdered sugar in two batches.
Mix in lemon juice and beat 2 minutes until light and fluffy.
Pipe frosting in a tall swirl on each cooled cupcake.
Top with a pinch of fresh lemon zest before serving.
tips: Use fresh lemon juice, not bottled, for the brightest flavor.
Zest your lemons before juicing them, it is much easier that way.
Let cupcakes cool completely before frosting or the swirl will slide.
If frosting looks too soft, chill it 10 minutes before piping.

faq.question: Can I make these cupcakes ahead of time?
faq.answer: Yes, bake the cupcakes up to 2 days ahead and store unfrosted at room temperature in an airtight container. Frost them the day you plan to serve for the best swirl.

faq.question: Why is my lemon frosting curdling or looking grainy?
faq.answer: This happens when the lemon juice is added too fast to cold butter. Add it slowly, one tablespoon at a time, while beating on low speed.

faq.question: Can I use bottled lemon juice instead of fresh?
faq.answer: Fresh juice gives a brighter, less bitter flavor and I recommend it here. Bottled juice will work in a pinch but the lemon taste will be milder.

faq.question: How do I get more lemonade flavor without making the batter too wet?
faq.answer: Add extra zest instead of more juice. Zest adds strong lemon flavor without changing the batter's liquid balance.

conclusion: These Summer Lemonade Cupcakes bring real lemon flavor to any warm day gathering. The tall frosting swirl and fresh zest make them look as bright as they taste.
